title: Pegboard spool holder: the A1's active spool, on the board
subtitle: One arm straight out of the board, spool face parallel to the board · 2 shared hook pegs + 2 pins (tools/pegboard.py) · your Menards 3/16" board · X out from the board, Z up · mm

meshes.label: Spool holder (2 hooks side by side, 2 pins 2" below, arm, end lip)
Reference 1 kg spool: 200 OD × 68 wide, 53 bore
Your board: Menards 3/16" white (6.35 mm holes, 3.94 mm thick)

scale_note: Real size. Pegs are the shared 6.1 mm hooks + pins. The spool is a typical 1 kg spool (200 mm across, 68 mm wide, 53 mm bore); the arm and lip pass through bores down to 50 mm and hold spools up to 82 mm wide.
notes: v2: two hooks side by side in the same row (1" apart), with two pins 2 holes (2") below them, so four holes take the load and the part can't twist. Both hooks share the same rocking axis, so it still goes on like one hook: tilt it, push both hook tips up through the holes, swing the bottom in. The arm is now 31.5 mm wide so it spans both columns and sits centred between the hooks. Printing: on its side, as before, but only one column of pegs can touch the bed. The other column's pegs are 25 mm up and need supports (tree, on build plate only). Still to check: (1) which holes behind the A1 (the bed slides toward the board, and the spool stands 74 mm out); (2) whether the filament reaches the A1's PTFE tube; (3) fixed arm OK, or a spinning hub on 608 bearings?
